handoff.objective: Attempt to convert PROP-701-I's QUALITATIVE group-growth argument into a QUANTITATIVE LOWER BOUND on the branching factor B that a bounded-branching per-word projection must pay for a given entropy loss across Phi = ARK . MC . SR, and report either the bound with its full cost accounting or a precise statement of why the argument does not yield one. THE OBJECT, stated exactly so it is not drifted from. Let F = GF(2^8), let pi : F^4 -> X be a per-word projection with ENTROPY LOSS L = 32 - log2|X| bits, applied at every super-box word. PROP-701-I assumes pi propagates DETERMINISTICALLY: there exist functions F_j : X^4 -> X with pi(word_j(Phi(s))) = F_j(pi(word_0(s)),...,pi(word_3(s))) for EVERY state s. OD-4 DROPS DETERMINISM to BOUNDED BRANCHING: relations R_j subset X^4 x X with |R_j(x)| <= B for every x, such that pi(word_j(Phi(s))) is in R_j(pi(word_0(s)),...,pi(word_3(s))) for every state s. B = 1 recovers PROP-701-I exactly, and PROP-701-I says NOTHING about B > 1. THE QUESTION: does the Step-1/Step-2/Step-3 machinery, run with B > 1, force an inequality relating B, L and the number of interfaces n over which the object must survive -- of the shape 'to sustain L bits of loss across n interfaces, B must be at least f(L, n)' -- and does the resulting per-attempt cost B^n times the inverse success probability of following the object beat the trivial alternative at any in-scope round count? A CLEAN, ARGUED 'NO SUCH BOUND FOLLOWS, AND HERE IS THE EXACT STEP THAT BREAKS AND WHY' IS A COMPLETE AND VALUABLE OUTCOME AND IS REPORTED AS THE RESULT, NOT AS A FAILURE. Manufacturing a bound that does not follow would be far worse than returning none.
